zh: 第二、明正相者，若動觸發時，無向二十惡法，具足十種善法。十種善法者：一、觸相如法；二、定相如法；三、空相如法；四、明相如法；五、喜相如法；六、樂相如法；七、善相如法；八、智相如法；九、解脫相如法；十、心調相如法。云何名如法？若與二十不善相法相違，安隱清淨，調和中適，即是如法，名為正相。是事至後第七大段，明證根本初禪覺支中當分別其相。如一動觸正相如是，餘七觸正相皆類之可知。
en: Second, clarifying the correct marks: if, when the tactile sensation of movement arises, none of the twenty unwholesome dharmas given above is present, and all ten kinds of wholesome dharma are present in full. The ten kinds of wholesome dharma are: the mark of the sensation itself in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of concentration in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of emptiness in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of brightness in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of joy in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of pleasure in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of wholesomeness in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of wisdom in accordance with the Dharma; the mark of liberation in accordance with the Dharma; and the mark of a well-regulated mind in accordance with the Dharma. What is meant by "in accordance with the Dharma"? Whatever runs contrary to the twenty unwholesome marks given above, at peace and pure, harmonized and moderate — this is precisely what is meant by "in accordance with the Dharma," and is called the correct mark. This matter will be distinguished further below, in the seventh great section, within the clarification of realizing the awakening-factors of the root first dhyāna. Just as the correct marks within this single tactile sensation of movement are as described, the correct marks within the remaining seven sensations may all be understood by the same pattern.

zh: 問曰：是中一向但逐事說，若隨此相分別，是邪是正，是偽是真，是應捨是應取，豈非顛倒憶想，墮邪僻耶？答曰：正有二種：一、世間正；二、出世間正。若如世間善法相而說，即是世間正相；出世間解脫善法相而說，即是出世間正相。今明根本觸中十種正相，即是辯世間正也，如《摩訶衍論》云：「因世間正見，得出世正見。若破世間正見，即破出世正見。」是故今欲明出世正法，必須先明世間正法。欲因事顯理，借近明遠故，須先分別根本事中初觸正相。
en: Question: throughout this, one has spoken only in terms of concrete phenomena — if one distinguishes what is deviant and what is correct, what is false and what is genuine, what should be rejected and what should be taken up, simply by following these marks, is this not itself a kind of inverted, deluded thinking, falling into deviance? Answer: "correct" is of two kinds — worldly correctness, and world-transcending correctness. Speaking in terms of the marks of worldly wholesome dharmas, this is worldly correctness; speaking in terms of the marks of world-transcending, liberating wholesome dharmas, this is world-transcending correctness. What has been clarified here, the ten correct marks within the root tactile sensations, is precisely the distinguishing of worldly correctness. As the Mahāyāna treatise says: "Through worldly right view, world-transcending right view is attained. If worldly right view is destroyed, world-transcending right view is destroyed along with it." Hence, wishing now to clarify the world-transcending correct Dharma, one must first clarify the worldly correct Dharma. Wishing to disclose principle through phenomena, borrowing the near at hand to illuminate the far, one must first distinguish the correct mark of the initial tactile sensation within the root, phenomenal dhyāna.

zh: 復次，若觸內發時，或見三十六物，或發慈心因緣，正智念佛等諸餘禪定。若有功德安隱如法，資益觸樂，亦是宿世善根發，各有十種正相，並是正定。但欲修根本禪定成就者，悉不得取是相，若謝、不謝，於根本禪無所妨也。然末世行者善根微薄，證觸之時，多不發諸餘事理。禪中境界，今恐有發者不識故，略出此意。餘十四門禪發正相亦當如是，一一自類廣分別之。
en: Furthermore: when the tactile sensation arises inwardly, one may also see the thirty-six substances, or bring forth loving-kindness, causation, right wisdom, buddha-recollection, and the other dhyāna-concentrations. If there is genuine merit, peace, and accordance with the Dharma, aiding and enriching the joy of the sensation, this too is the arising of a wholesome root from past lives, each of these likewise having its own ten correct marks, and all of them being right concentration. But for one who wishes to cultivate the root dhyānas to their own completion, none of these marks should be seized upon — whether they pass away or do not pass away makes no difference to the root dhyāna's own progress. In this latter age, however, practitioners' wholesome roots are thin and slight, and, at the moment the tactile sensation is realized, most do not bring forth these other phenomenal or principled states within dhyāna at all; fearing that some who do bring them forth might fail to recognize them, this point is given here in brief. The correct marks arising within the remaining fourteen gates of dhyāna should likewise each be distinguished at length, each according to its own kind.

The ten right marks are defined mainly by contrast with the twenty wrong ones, with only a brief positive description — "peaceful and pure, harmonized and balanced" — and their fuller treatment deferred to the seventh great section. The text itself flags a limitation: this is only "worldly correctness," a coarse phenomenal check, not yet the "world-transcending correctness" of liberating wisdom. The citation from the Mahāyāna treatise (worldly right view as the very foundation world-transcending right view depends on) is the treatise's justification for spending so much space on something as seemingly mundane as bodily sensations during sitting: getting the near, concrete case right is what makes it possible to trust the same diagnostic instinct when it is later turned on far subtler, more abstract objects.

zh: 第二、明以法驗知邪正者，自有邪禪，其相微細難別，與正禪相似，非則相之所能別，應以三法驗知：一、定心研磨；二、用本法修治；三、智慧破析。如《涅槃經》說：「欲知真金，應三種試之，謂燒、打、磨。」行人亦是，難可別識。若欲別之，亦須三種試之，所謂當與共事；共事不知，當與久處；久處不知，以智慧觀察。今借此意以明禪定邪、正之相。
en: Second, clarifying how to verify the deviant from the correct by means of the dharma: there exist deviant dhyānas whose marks are so subtle and fine, so difficult to distinguish, so closely resembling a genuine dhyāna, that marks alone cannot tell them apart; one should verify them instead by three methods: settling the mind deep in concentration and refining it there; treating it by cultivating the very method through which it arose; and analyzing it through wisdom. As the Nirvāṇa Sūtra says: "To know true gold, one should test it three ways — by burning, striking, and polishing." A practitioner is exactly the same, difficult to recognize. If one wishes to distinguish such a person, one likewise needs three tests: one should work together with them; if working together does not reveal them, one should dwell with them for a long time; if dwelling with them for a long time does not reveal them, one should observe them through wisdom. Here, this same sense is borrowed to clarify the deviant and correct marks of dhyāna-concentration.

zh: 如發一動觸，若邪正未了，應當深入定心，於所發境中不取不捨，但平心定住。若是善根定力踰深，善根踰發，若魔所為，不久自壞。二、以本法修治，如發不淨觀禪，還修不淨觀，隨所修時，境界增明，此則非偽。若以本修治，漸漸壞滅，當知即是邪相。三、以智慧觀察者，觀所發法，推檢根源，不見生處，深知空寂，心不住著，邪當自滅，正當自顯。如燒真金，益其光色；若是偽金，即自黑壞。如此簡別，以三法驗之，邪正可知。定譬於磨，修治喻打，智慧觀察，類以火燒。又復久處喻磨，共事如打，火燒即譬智慧觀察。餘禪定例爾驗之，邪正可知。
en: For instance, when the tactile sensation of movement arises, if the deviant and the correct are not yet clear, one should enter deeply into the concentrated mind, neither taking up nor rejecting whatever state has arisen, simply settling the mind in equanimity. If it is a genuine wholesome root, the power of concentration will grow ever deeper and the wholesome root ever more manifest; if it is the work of a demon, it will, before long, collapse of itself.

Second, treating it by cultivating the very method through which it arose: for instance, if the contemplation of impurity itself arises, one returns to cultivating the contemplation of impurity — if, as one cultivates it, the state grows ever clearer and brighter, this is not false. But if, through cultivating the very method, it gradually collapses and dissolves instead, one should know that this is precisely a deviant mark.

Third, observing it through wisdom: one observes the dharma that has arisen, tracing and examining it back to its root source, and, finding no place where it truly arises, coming to know deeply that it is empty and still, the mind no longer abiding in or clinging to it — the deviant will then vanish of itself, and the correct will then manifest of itself. It is just like burning true gold: this only increases its own light and color; but if it is false gold, it turns black and crumbles of itself. Distinguishing them in this way, verifying them through these three methods, the deviant and the correct can be known. Settling the mind in concentration is comparable to polishing; treating it through the original method is comparable to striking; and observing it through wisdom is comparable to burning with fire. And again: dwelling with a person for a long time is comparable to polishing, working together with them is like striking, and burning with fire is precisely comparable to observing through wisdom. Every other dhyāna-concentration should be verified after this same pattern, and the deviant and the correct can then be known.

The double analogy — three tests for knowing a practitioner (work together, dwell together over time, observe through wisdom) mapped onto three tests for genuine gold (burn, strike, polish), both then mapped onto the three verification methods themselves — is characteristic of the treatise's method of borrowing everyday similes to secure something otherwise hard to pin down in words. What all three methods share is a refusal to judge from the content of the experience alone: settling into equanimity, returning to the original practice, and analytic wisdom all work by seeing what a state does under pressure over time, not what it looks like in the moment.

zh: 二、簡是魔非魔，即為二意：一、明是魔相；二、明非魔相。今明魔禪有二種不同：一、明禪非是魔，魔入禪中。如行者於正心中發諸禪定，惡魔恐其道高，為作惱亂，入其禪中，若心貪著，或生憂懼，即魔得其便。若能如上用心却之，魔邪既滅，如雲除日顯，定心明淨。二、明一向魔作禪定誑惑行者，若覺知非真，用法治之，魔退之後，則無復毫釐禪法。
en: Second, discriminating whether something is demonic or not: this itself has two parts — clarifying the marks of what is genuinely demonic; and clarifying the marks of what is not demonic. Here, two differing kinds of "demonic dhyāna" are clarified.

First, clarifying that the dhyāna itself is not demonic, but a demon has entered into it: as when a practitioner, within a correctly settled mind, brings forth the various dhyāna-concentrations, and an evil demon, fearing that the practitioner's path is growing too exalted, seeks to cause disturbance by entering into that very dhyāna — if the mind then grows attached and clinging, or gives rise to worry and fear, the demon thereby gains its opening. But if one is able to use the mind as described above to repel it, the demonic deviance is dispelled, just as clouds part to reveal the sun, and the concentrated mind grows bright and pure once more.

Second, clarifying dhyāna that is, from the very start, entirely the work of a demon, deceiving and confusing the practitioner: if one recognizes that it is not genuine and treats it by the methods given, then, once the demon has withdrawn, not the slightest trace of any dhyāna-dharma remains at all.

zh: 次明非魔相者，罪障於禪，似如魔作，理實非魔，難可別識。若用前所說却之，終不得去，若能勤修懺悔，罪既除滅，則禪定自然分明。復次，或入定時，方便不巧，致令境界不如法，若更善作方便，則所證明淨，故知非魔之所作也。
en: Next, clarifying what is not, in fact, demonic: a karmic offense obstructing the dhyāna may resemble the work of a demon, while, in actual principle, it is not demonic at all — and this is difficult to distinguish. If one uses the methods given above to repel it, it will, in the end, never depart; but if one is able to diligently cultivate repentance, once the offense is removed and extinguished, the dhyāna-concentration will naturally grow clear of itself. Furthermore: at times, when entering concentration, one's skillful means may simply be unskillful, causing the resulting state to fail to accord with the Dharma; if one instead applies skillful means properly, what is then realized will be clear and pure — hence it should be known that this, too, is not the work of any demon.

This closing distinction is a diagnostic safety valve: not every obstruction that looks demonic actually is one, and treating a karmic-offense obstruction with anti-demon methods will simply fail, while treating it with repentance succeeds — the very failure of the "wrong" remedy becomes part of how the two are told apart. Together with the "killer" etymology and persistence-test given earlier for wholesome-root marks, this closes the treatise's first sustained treatment of demonic interference, though the topic returns with its own full chapter as the fifth and final internal-expedient-means layer, recognizing demonic affairs (覺魔事). This closes the third of verifying wholesome capacity's four parts.

items.en: Distinguishing That Dhyāna's Arising Is Not Fixed

zh: 第四、次料揀發禪不定，略為五意：一、正料揀事、理兩修發禪不定；二、明發禪所由；三、辨發禪多少；四、明發宿善根盡相；五、約有漏、無漏分別。
en: Fourth, next distinguishing that dhyāna's arising through this is not fixed: in brief, this has five parts — directly distinguishing that dhyāna's arising through both phenomenal and principle cultivation is not fixed; clarifying the reasons dhyāna arises at all; distinguishing how much dhyāna arises; clarifying whether one's wholesome roots from past lives are exhausted; and distinguishing this in terms of the contaminated and the uncontaminated.

quiz.q: What does "in accordance with the Dharma" mean for the ten correct marks?
options: the stronger the pleasure the better
contrary to the twenty unwholesome marks, at peace and pure, harmonized and moderate
quiz.why: "What is meant by 'in accordance with the Dharma'? Whatever runs contrary to the twenty unwholesome marks given above, at peace and pure, harmonized and moderate — this is precisely what is meant by 'in accordance with the Dharma,' and is called the correct mark."

quiz.q: It is objected that judging by marks is itself inverted thinking. How does the text answer?
options: correctness is worldly and world-transcending; these ten are worldly; "through worldly right view, world-transcending right view is attained"
quiz.why: "'Correct' is of two kinds — worldly correctness, and world-transcending correctness ... the ten correct marks within the root tactile sensations, is precisely the distinguishing of worldly correctness. As the Mahāyāna treatise says: 'Through worldly right view, world-transcending right view is attained.'"

quiz.q: Which three methods are used in dharma-verification?
options: refining in the concentrated mind, treating by the original method, analyzing through wisdom
quiz.why: "One should verify them instead by three methods: settling the mind deep in concentration and refining it there; treating it by cultivating the very method through which it arose; and analyzing it through wisdom."

quiz.q: The Nirvāṇa Sūtra's three tests of gold are matched to the three verifications. Which pairing is correct?
options: concentration burning, treatment polishing, wisdom striking
concentration is polishing, treatment by method is striking, observation through wisdom is burning
concentration striking, treatment burning, wisdom polishing
quiz.why: "Settling the mind in concentration is comparable to polishing; treating it through the original method is comparable to striking; and observing it through wisdom is comparable to burning with fire."

quiz.q: In refining through the concentrated mind, how do the results differ for a wholesome root and for a demon's work?
options: if wholesome, concentration deepens and the root grows; if demonic, it soon collapses of itself
quiz.why: "One should enter deeply into the concentrated mind, neither taking up nor rejecting whatever state has arisen, simply settling the mind in equanimity. If it is a genuine wholesome root, the power of concentration will grow ever deeper and the wholesome root ever more manifest; if it is the work of a demon, it will, before long, collapse of itself."

quiz.q: What two kinds of "demonic dhyāna" does the text distinguish?
options: the dhyāna is not demonic but a demon enters it; the dhyāna is from the start entirely a demon's deception
quiz.why: "First, clarifying that the dhyāna itself is not demonic, but a demon has entered into it ... Second, clarifying dhyāna that is, from the very start, entirely the work of a demon ... once the demon has withdrawn, not the slightest trace of any dhyāna-dharma remains at all."

quiz.q: What is "not demonic," and how is it treated?
options: a karmic offense obstructing dhyāna that resembles a demon; repelling it fails, but diligent repentance removes it and dhyāna becomes clear
quiz.why: "A karmic offense obstructing the dhyāna may resemble the work of a demon, while, in actual principle, it is not demonic at all ... If one uses the methods given above to repel it, it will, in the end, never depart; but if one is able to diligently cultivate repentance, once the offense is removed and extinguished, the dhyāna-concentration will naturally grow clear of itself."
